subject: Discrete-time, multi-state CJS model with uneven time intervals

messages.author: 00d4a4fc726d0cad
messages.subject: Discrete-time, multi-state CJS model with uneven time intervals
parts:
Hi Folks,

I’m working on a discrete-time multi-state extension of the Cormack-Jolly-Seber survival model, similar to examples in Ch. 9 of Kéry and Schaub 2012. However, the time intervals of surveys are not evenly spaced. Surveys were conducted at approximately 6-month time intervals but can vary from 5 to 7 months. To account for this I’ve made a simple adjustment using exponentiation of each survival parameter (phi[i,t], where i is an individual and t is a time step) by the number of months (months[t]) between surveys for each time interval, for example phi[i,t]^months[t], thereby obtaining monthly survival estimates (attached ...-months.R).

Does this seem like a reasonable approach to deal with uneven time intervals? Are there pitfalls to using this approach? The results appear similar when I derive survival parameters for 6 months compared to the model that does not account for the length of time intervals. I am looking to avoid continuous-time survival models for now.

Thanks in advance for any insights,

Brian
